svg.text: MySQL binary log
Kafka Connect + Debezium
Event router
Kafka event streams
Change-data capture (Fig 6-4)
tail the log (MySQL binary log, PostgreSQL write-ahead log),
convert each change to an event; every change is seen;
fields configurable (metadata such as serverId, transactionId);
checkpoint progress; at-least-once is fine since entity
updates are idempotent; MongoDB Change Streams, Couchbase
Snapshotting (bootstrapping)
the log keeps only a short window, so load the current data
from the store, then switch to the log with overlap;
a big query may lock a production table for hours;
options: read-only replica, or Debezium's incremental
snapshot (Netflix DBLog watermarks, no locks, chunked)
Benefits of log-based CDC
delete tracking (to tombstones); minimal data store impact
(change tables as in SQL Server add load by volume);
low latency; non-blocking snapshots
Drawbacks of log-based CDC
exposes the internal data model; denormalisation must happen
downstream (normalised streams, foreign-key joins, Chapter 7);
brittle dependency between source and event schema
